items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: The interviewee narrates stories about Yank in the third person (e.g., 'Yank was playing for Louis', 'Yank was learning playing horned in') and does not claim a direct personal interaction or relationship with Yank himself.

ctx.x: Chook? Chook. Chook. That's what his name is, Chook. I don't know what his name is.
Chook. Chook. You take Lundy. You take Harrison Lundy, Bill Lundy, Boogerman Lundy, Yank didn't Lundy because Buddy wouldn't name him at home. He'd learn from Chook home, Yank. Oh yeah.
He did, yeah, because he used to follow us every Saturday night. Chook. I was playing in Gretna.

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: Yanky was a tough trombone player. He was tough. You could stand near and eat at Cornhole Street and say, oh, that was Yanky.

ctx.x: How did Yank sound, did he?
Oh, Yanky. Yanky was a tough trombone player. He was tough. You could stand near and eat at Cornhole Street and say, oh, that was Yanky.
